stem:
A 26-year-old sees her GP four months before she plans to conceive. She takes carbamazepine for epilepsy and has never had a pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect. She asks which folic acid to start.

What should the GP prescribe?

options.label: A
options.text: 400 micrograms daily, because she has no previous affected pregnancy
options.explanation: 400 micrograms is the usual-risk dose. Carbamazepine is a reason for the higher dose even when no previous pregnancy was affected.

options.label: B
options.text: 5 mg daily, but only after a pregnancy test is positive
options.explanation: The higher dose is right, but waiting for a positive test misses the weeks when the neural tube closes.

options.label: C
options.text: 5 mg daily, starting now, before she conceives
options.explanation: An anticonvulsant puts her in the high-risk group. The GP prescribes 5 mg folic acid daily, started before conception.

options.label: D
options.text: No tablet. A varied diet covers an anticonvulsant
options.explanation: Diet does not replace the high-risk dose while she is taking carbamazepine.

options.label: E
options.text: 5 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth
options.explanation: Starting at 12 weeks is after neural-tube closure. The 5 mg dose has to be in place before she conceives.

context: Carbamazepine is a high-risk indication for folic acid 5 mg daily, started before conception.
